# PaRaMetriC

## Snapshot

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | Joint research project of the European Partnership on Metrology (EPM), project 21GRD03, co-financed by Horizon Europe and the participating states |
| **Coordination** | INRIM, Istituto Nazionale di Ricerca Metrologica (Turin, Italy) |
| **Goal** | A metrological framework for comparable performance assessment of passive radiative cooling (PRC) technologies |
| **Consortium** | 17 partners: national metrology and designated institutes, research centres and universities, and companies |
| **Official site** | [parametric.inrim.it](https://parametric.inrim.it/) |

## Why it matters for emissivity

A passive radiative cooler only works as well as its spectral properties
allow: high reflectance in the solar range and high emissivity in the
atmospheric window around 8–13 µm. That makes emissivity and reflectance
metrology the foundation of any fair comparison between cooling materials.
PaRaMetriC's objectives include performance-assessment standards, validated
models linking cooling performance to material properties, accurate methods
for thermophysical properties, and on-site test protocols with a target
uncertainty below 10 %.

Unlike [TAMARYS](/network/networks/tamarys.html), PaRaMetriC is a
fixed-term project consortium rather than an open network. It is listed here
because its partners and results sit at the heart of emissivity metrology.

## On the research map

Consortium partners with a research-map profile:

- [PTB — Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt](/network/ptb.html)
- [Center for Applied Energy Research (CAE)](/network/cae-wuerzburg.html)
- [TÜBİTAK UME](/network/tubitak-ume.html)

Other partners: INRIM, Aalto University, CMI, CSIC, DFM, LNE, RISE, CNR, FIW
München, NKUA Athens and Politecnico di Torino, plus the companies Almeco,
Cooling Photonics and CTI. See the project's
[consortium page](https://parametric.inrim.it/consortium).

The engineered-emissivity laboratories on the map (see
[ecosystems](/network/ecosystems.html)) are the natural users of the
framework PaRaMetriC is building.
